issues.description: Rideable.messageOnRide is specified without parameters in the UML/problem statement (`messageOnRide(): String`), but the solution defines it with a parameter (`messageOnRide(int speed)`). As a result, Pig and Seal implement `messageOnRide(int)` instead of the required `messageOnRide()`, so students following the statement will produce code incompatible with the reference solution (and any tests based on the spec).
issues.suggestedFix: Make all artifacts consistent. Preferred: change the solution to match the spec/UML by updating `Rideable` to `String messageOnRide();` and updating `Pig`/`Seal` to implement `messageOnRide()` with no parameters. If `speed` is intended, update the UML, problem statement text, and example usage accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement requires `messageOnRide()` to return exactly `"Riding on [Animal Type] [name]"`, but the solution's Pig/Seal ride messages include additional speed text (e.g., `"Riding on Pig <name> at <speed> mph"`). Even if the signature were corrected, this output-format mismatch would cause students to implement a different string than the reference solution/spec expects.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the solution to return exactly `"Riding on Pig " + getName()` / `"Riding on Seal " + getName()` (and remove speed text). If speed output is intended, update the problem statement to specify the speed suffix and show the parameter in the required method signature.
